claims.statement: The word in a question about a filmed crash influenced later speed estimates
claims.caveat: 1974 Exp I 45 students/7 films; first unprompted description then wording manipulation; answer effect does not prove trace overwrite

claims.statement: Later absent-glass yes/no responses differed between smashed and hit wording
claims.caveat: Exp II separate N=150; one-week glass responses smashed 16/50, hit 7/50, controls 6/50; later yes/no report not direct memory trace

claims.statement: The 1974 effect proves people always believe leading questions
claims.caveat: overgeneralization

claims.statement: The 1978 slides experiments totaled 1242 across five experiments plus a pilot
claims.caveat: 1242 across pilot+five experiments; pilot 129, Exp I 195; do not treat as one condition

claims.statement: 1978 misleading verbal information reduced recognition accuracy on two test types
claims.caveat: 1978 Exp I consistent 75% vs misleading 41% correct forced-choice; pilot yes/no design separate; no effort manipulation

claims.statement: Misinformation effects may depend on conditions and warnings are limited
claims.caveat: not all individuals or warnings

claims.statement: Loftus's work proves Puységur's witnesses were deceived
claims.caveat: no retrospective individual diagnosis

claims.statement: Coué used 20 knots for morning/evening counting in 1922 English edition
claims.caveat: instructions not clinical results

claims.statement: Puységur's case material dates to eighteenth-century 1780s
claims.caveat: not nineteenth

claims.statement: Wood self-statements tested Coué's exact method
claims.caveat: different procedures/outcomes/populations

claims.statement: Wood experiments included 249 survey, 68 repetition comparison, 116 analyzed online
claims.caveat: undergraduate and selection restrictions, immediate mood/state self-esteem

claims.statement: Repeated statements can influence perceived truth under study conditions
claims.caveat: not proof that repetition changes medical outcomes
